reason: The text explicitly contains a passage where the Israelite foremen confront Moses and Aaron after they exit from Pharaoh's presence. The foremen state: 'May the Lord look upon you and judge, because you have made us abhorrent in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us' (וַיִּפְגְּעוּ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹן... וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם יֵרֶא יְהוָה עֲלֵיכֶם וְיִשְׁפֹּט אֲשֶׁר הִבְאַשְׁתֶּם אֶת־ רֵיחֵנוּ בְּעֵינֵי פַרְעֹה וּבְעֵינֵי עֲבָדָיו לָתֶת־ חֶרֶב בְּיָדָם לְהָרְגֵֽנוּ). This directly demonstrates the Hebrew people blaming their leaders for putting them at mortal risk through their diplomatic approach to Pharaoh.
